questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: "Where do you live?" he asked.
o: He asked me where do I live.
He asked me where I live.
questions.x: In indirect questions, the question mark is removed, and the auxiliary verb shifts to the end of the clause.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech? "I have finished my work," he said.
o: He said that he has finished his work.
He said that he had finished his work.
He said he finished his work.
He said that he was finishing his work.
questions.x: The present perfect tense ('have finished') changes to past perfect ('had finished') in indirect speech.

questions.q: Choose the correct direct speech for: She asked me if I knew the answer.
o: "Do you know the answer?" she asked me.
"Did you know the answer?" she asked me.
"Do I know the answer?" she asked.
"Did I know the answer?" she asked me.
questions.x: The indirect question retains the same tense and structure as the direct question, with the subject and verb in present form.

questions.q: Which option correctly converts the indirect speech into direct speech? The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
o: "The earth revolves around the sun," said the teacher.
"The earth revolved around the sun," said the teacher.
"The earth is revolving around the sun," the teacher said.
"The earth revolves around the sun," the teacher says.
questions.x: Universal truths and statements of fact retain their tense in both direct and indirect speech.

questions.q: Identify the correct indirect speech for: "What a beautiful day!" he exclaimed.
o: He exclaimed that what a beautiful day it was.
He exclaimed that it was a beautiful day.
He exclaimed what a beautiful day.
He exclaimed that it was what a beautiful day.
questions.x: Exclamations in direct speech are converted to statements in indirect speech, with appropriate grammatical adjustments.

questions.q: Which phrase means 'to be extremely happy'?
questions.x: 'On cloud nine' is a well-known idiom meaning extreme happiness or euphoria.

questions.q: What does 'to hit the books' mean?
questions.x: It refers to studying or reading diligently, often in preparation for an exam.

questions.q: What does 'to let the cat out of the bag' mean?
questions.x: It means to accidentally or intentionally disclose a secret.

questions.q: Which phrase means 'to be very angry'?
o: Cost an arm and a leg
questions.x: 'See red' is an idiom meaning to become very angry.

questions.q: What does 'to break the ice' mean?
o: To start a conversation in a formal gathering
questions.x: It means to initiate conversation in a social setting to reduce initial awkwardness.

questions.q: Which idiom means 'to be in a difficult situation'?
o: Between the devil and the deep blue sea
questions.x: It describes being forced to choose between two equally bad options.

questions.q: What does 'to cost an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.x: It means something is very costly or priced too high.
